designs.title: No.
designs.why: Strong one-ink idea that reads from 3 m: a smug cat lying on a ledge over a heavy 'NO' and casually pawing the full stop like a ball. Clean, confident line weights, the hatched tail and striped letters give texture without a second colour, and it inverts well onto the black tee. Production nits: the white stripe cuts in the letters are uneven, and the shortest ones are thin slivers at the stroke edges that will fill in or go ragged on press. The whiskers and fine tail hatching are near the minimum width at print size. The ledge line is doubled and wobbly where it meets the letters, and the stop reads more as a ball than as a full stop.
designs.fix: Redraw the letter stripes as fewer, consistent cuts that run fully through each stroke, at least about 1 mm wide, and drop the edge slivers. Bring the whiskers and tail hatching up to a safe minimum of about 0.5 pt / 0.4 mm. That way the black-ink and white-on-black versions both hold up without dot gain or fill-in.
